dct_description_sm: New research is required to improve management in BB.  At the same time, research methods previously used to study polar bears - specifically physical mark-recapture - have faced criticism from Inuit over concerns about chemical immobilization and handling. While these concerns do not necessarily preclude the use of physical mark-recapture to assess the Baffin Bay sub-population, it has stimulated interest in the development of alternative, less invasive techniques. The GN Department of Environment (DoE) has responded by using biopsy darting to conduct a genetic mark-recapture study. This research does not require the capture or handling of bears. Recent testing including success in Baffin Bay in 2011 and 2012 suggests the method is viable for polar bears. Here, we propose to undertake a 3-year genetic mark-recapture study using biopsy darting to sample polar bears along the east coast of Baffin Island during late summer and fall in 2011-2013. In addition to providing an estimate of the population size, the study will yield polar bear demographic and distribution data. Objectives: 1)  To estimate the current size and composition of polar bears in Baffin Bay (BB), 2)  To compare a new estimate of abundance with those derived from past study in-order to gain insight into population trend and status in BB, 3)  To estimate survival and reproductive parameters (to the extent possible) in-order to facilitate population viability analyses, 4)  To evaluate polar bear distribution during the period of minimum sea-ice with respect to environmental variables, particularly ice conditions, topography and food availability distribution, and 5)  To demonstrate the utility of genetic mark-recapture as a less invasive alternative to physical capture for the purpose of population monitoring.
